title: api-schema-versioning: add beta headers and backward-compat shims for request/response schemas
author: Maya Singh
description: Background: We need a migration path for clients as we evolve the API request/response schemas to support structured output, improved tool/function-calling hooks, and streaming stability. Breaking changes risk destabilizing downstream integrations and the OpenAI-compat layer users. This PR introduces a versioning header (Redwood-API-Version / Redwood-API-Beta), deprecation metadata in responses, and inbound/outbound shims to preserve behavior for older clients. Scope: - Add support for Redwood-API-Version header and Redwood-API-Beta boolean header to opt into preview behaviors. - Emit response-level metadata (x-redwood-deprecation, redwood-schema-version) for clients to detect and log deprecated fields. - Implement server-side request shims to accept legacy fields (e.g., `tool_call` -> new `function_call` shape) and map them to the canonical internal schema. - Add response shims to translate new structured output into legacy OpenAI-compatible shapes when client opts out via headers. - Update OpenAI compatibility layer to respect headers and prefer compatibility shims when requested. - Add docs and changelog entries. Motivation: We must be able to iterate on schema improvements (structured output, stronger typing for tool calling, stable chunked streaming) without forcing a hard cutover. The headers allow gradual opt-in to new beta features and explicit client awareness of deprecations. Checklist: - [x] API header parsing and validation - [x] Request shims for legacy fields - [x] Response shims for backward compatibility - [x] Response deprecation metadata and schema versioning field - [x] Tests: unit and integration + e2e through OpenAI-compat shim - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] CI green on rerun Changes (high level): - server/api/versioning.py: new header parsing and version negotiation flow - server/api/shims.py: request and response translation utilities, mapping tables for legacy field names - server/compat/openai_adapter.py: respect Redwood-API-* headers and use shims when needed - server/streaming/chunker.py: minor adjustments to preserve stream chunk semantics across compatibility translations - docs/api/versioning.md: migration guide and examples - tests/{unit,integration}/test_api_versioning.py: coverage for negotiation and shims Compatibility guarantees: - Default behavior for clients without Redwood-API-Version remains unchanged. - Clients sending Redwood-API-Beta: true receive new structured output and function-calling signatures. - Clients sending Redwood-API-Version: 2026-02 receive a stable documented schema; higher versions may include additional fields. - When Redwood-API-Beta is not present, server applies response shims to keep the OpenAI-compatible shapes (legacy `tool_call` fields retained). Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; monitor error rates and compatibility telemetry for one week. 2) Enable widely and announce migration timeline (ENG-4923). 3) Deprecation warnings emitted for legacy fields for 90 days before removal. Testing notes: - Integration tests simulate both legacy and beta clients. - Ran compatibility e2e using redwood-openai-compat with sample prompts and functions. - Streaming tests ensure chunk boundaries preserved when shims rewrite payloads. Related: ENG-4923 (schema versioning), ENG-4978 (openai compat updates), SUP-214 (customer reported tool_call mismatch).

release_notes:
- Introduces Redwood-API-Version and Redwood-API-Beta request headers for schema version negotiation and opt-in previews.
- Adds backward-compatible request/response shims so older clients continue to work while we iterate on structured output and function-calling shapes.
- Emits deprecation metadata and redwood-schema-version in responses to enable instrumented migrations.
